dailyInsight.headline: Audit whether a denied agent response can still reach session history
dailyInsight.insight: Microsoft Agent Framework's fresh experimental Agent Hooks work supports one bounded audit for teams that apply policy after model or tool work begins: trace a rejected response through both the user-facing stream and the state a later turn can load. Its source change puts verdict-gated persistence beside the output gate, so the intended question is not only whether a deny hides text now, but whether the denied text becomes durable context later.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public implementation joins agent, model, and function interception as one middleware bundle, fails closed on enforcement-layer errors, buffers streams until the relevant verdicts have run, and defers the covered history write until that verdict permits it. Its focused tests include denied streams, denied output without durable history, transformed output persistence, and retries. The source also documents that provider-hosted tools do not take the direct function-invocation path.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: An agent's session memory is part of its future authority: text that is blocked at egress but retained in history can still shape a later model call, handoff, summary, or operator review. Auditing both boundaries gives a team a testable way to distinguish a visible moderation result from actual containment of the rejected material.

actions.audience: Framework builder or operator responsible for agent policy and session persistence
actions.label: Run one deny-to-memory test
actions.instruction: In a disposable environment with non-sensitive prompts, cause one post-model or output policy deny. Verify separately that no partial stream reached the client and that the next run, session reload, summary, or delegated task cannot retrieve the denied material. Repeat after one retry path. Record any provider-hosted tool path that bypasses your direct tool interceptor; do not infer coverage from a visible deny alone.

receipts.title: Python: agent-hooks interception contract as a first-class experimental core feature (#7515)
receipts.supports: Shows the experimental middleware integration, verdict-gated output and history behavior, stated hosted-tool limitation, and focused regression tests for denied streams, persistence, transformed output, nested runs, and retries.

confidence.basis: One fresh public Agent Framework commit, its implementation paths, and focused tests agree on the narrow deny-to-history mechanism; the surrounding Agent Hooks contract supplies the stated control model and caveat.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are public source and test receipts from an experimental implementation. They do not establish a released package, production deployment, independent security testing, conformance certification, or complete mediation of provider-hosted tool execution.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public regression evidence shows that a denied response still enters the covered history provider or a later session reload, if stream data escapes before the output verdict, or if the documented hosting boundary is materially broader than the source currently states.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a released integration, a current-draft conformance report, and tests that demonstrate how provider-hosted tools and long-lived nested sessions interact with the persistence gate.
